skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Automate Twitter/X tasks through the belt CLI, including posting, media posts, likes, retweets, direct messages, follows, profile lookup, and post lookup.
skill.summary: Run Twitter/X posting and engagement actions through inference.sh belt apps.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown wrapper around the belt CLI for Twitter/X automation. Several static backtick findings are Markdown false positives, but the real command examples can post, delete, like, retweet, message, follow, and install related skills. No prompt injection text was found, but automated engagement and messaging create a high-risk abuse path.

remediation.issue: Commands can mutate a connected Twitter/X account.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before posting, deleting, liking, retweeting, following, or sending direct messages.

remediation.issue: Direct message, follow, and engagement examples can enable spam or social engineering.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent, rate-limit, and policy checks. Remove language that promotes engagement bots or audience growth automation.

remediation.issue: Setup instructions use npx to install additional skills.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted package sources and versions. Ask users to review package provenance before running install commands.

content.value_statement: Managing Twitter/X actions by hand is slow and error prone. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code run approved belt CLI workflows for posts, media, and engagement.
actual_capabilities: Posts text updates to Twitter/X through the x/post-tweet app.
Creates media posts with the x/post-create app and a media URL.
Likes, retweets, deletes, and reads posts by tweet ID.
Sends direct messages to a specified recipient ID.
Follows users and retrieves profile data through belt apps.
Shows workflows for generating media with belt apps before posting.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Does not include built-in consent, rate-limit, or campaign approval checks.
Uses command examples only. It does not implement a native API client.
Twitter/X permissions and platform policies can limit or block actions.

use_cases.title: Publish Product Updates
use_cases.description: A product marketer can prepare approved text or media posts and publish them through the connected account.

use_cases.title: Manage Social Support Messages
use_cases.description: A support lead can send approved direct messages after confirming the recipient and message text.

use_cases.title: Inspect Account and Post Data
use_cases.description: A social analyst can retrieve post details or user profiles for manual review and reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Post a Simple Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Post this approved update to Twitter/X: [text]. Confirm the account and exact text before running the command.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Media Post
prompt_templates.scenario: Post with an existing media URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Twitter/X media post with this text and media URL: [text], [media URL]. Ask for confirmation before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Post Before Engagement
prompt_templates.prompt: Get details for tweet ID [id], summarize the content, then ask whether to like or retweet it.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Approved Campaign Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a sequence for posting, profile lookup, and one approved follow action. Require confirmation before every account-changing command.

output_examples.input: Post an approved launch message with a media URL.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the target account, repeats the exact post text, verifies the media URL, and waits for approval before publishing.

output_examples.input: Send a thank-you direct message to a customer.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for recipient confirmation, checks that the message is approved, and sends it only after explicit consent.

output_examples.input: Look up a public profile for reporting.
output_examples.output: The assistant retrieves the profile details and summarizes the relevant public information for the report.

best_practices: Confirm the connected account and exact action before every account-changing command.
Use approved copy, consent records, and platform policy checks for messages and follows.
Start with read-only profile or post lookup before liking, retweeting, deleting, or messaging.
anti_patterns: Do not automate unsolicited direct messages, bulk follows, or engagement farming.
Do not publish generated media or text without human review and rights checks.
Do not run install commands from unreviewed package sources or moving branches.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Twitter/X account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires belt CLI authentication and a connected Twitter/X integration with the needed permissions.

faq.question: Can it post media?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the x/post-create app with text and a media URL.

faq.question: Can it read posts and profiles?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for x/post-get and x/user-get through belt.

faq.question: Does it schedule posts automatically?
faq.answer: No built-in scheduler is shown. It provides command examples for immediate belt app actions.

faq.question: Is it safe for bulk engagement campaigns?
faq.answer: Use caution. Bulk likes, follows, retweets, and direct messages can violate policies and harm recipients.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, with belt CLI commands as the operating path.
